provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: The market
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state items sold in the market.
The pupils should be able to list different market items.

Introduction:
We go to market with our parents.
We see many things in the market.

Content:
Market is where we buy things.
People sell food, clothes, and toys.
Tomato costs 50 naira.
Rice is sold in big bags.
Mama Ngozi sells fish.
Papa Tunde sells yams.

Class activity:
Let's play market game.
Some pupils are sellers.
Others are buyers with toy money.

Evaluation questions:
Name three things sold in market.
How much does tomato cost?
Who sells fish in the market?

Summary:
Market is where we buy and sell things.

topics.title: Trades in my area
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name different trades.
The pupils should be able to explain what a carpenter does.

Introduction:
We see people working every day.
They have different jobs.

Content:
Carpenter makes tables and chairs.
Tailor makes clothes for us.
Trader sells things in the market.
Mama Ada is a tailor.
She sews our school uniform.
Pappa Emeka is a carpenter.
He fixes broken desks.

Class activity:
Let's pretend to be workers.
Some pupils will be carpenters.
Others will be tailors.

Evaluation questions:
What does a tailor do?
Name one trader you know.
Who makes furniture?

Summary:
People have different jobs to help us.

topics.title: Tools of workers
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify tools of workers.
The pupils should be able to match tools to workers.

Introduction:
Workers use special tools.
Tools help them do their work.

Content:
Carpenter uses saw and hammer.
Tailor uses scissors and needle.
Farmer uses hoe and cutlass.
Saw cuts wood into pieces.
Scissors cut cloth.
Hoe digs the ground.

Class activity:
Let's match tools to workers.
I will show a tool.
You say who uses it.

Evaluation questions:
What tool does a farmer use?
Name one tool for carpenter.
Who uses scissors?

Summary:
Each worker has special tools.

topics.title: Planting vegetables
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to plant maize seeds.
The pupils should be able to state how to care for plants.

Introduction:\ Plants need water to grow.
We can plant vegetables at home.

Content:
Maize has yellow seeds.
Beans are small and brown.
First dig small holes in soil.
Put seeds in holes.
Cover seeds with soil.
Water the plants every day.
Pull out weeds that grow.

Class activity:
Let's plant maize seeds.
Each pupil will plant one seed.
We will water our plants.

Evaluation questions:
What do plants need to grow?
How do we plant seeds?
Why do we pull weeds?

Summary:
We can plant and care for vegetables.

topics.title: Animals and their food
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list animals and their food.
The pupils should be able to match animals to what they eat.

Introduction:
Animals eat different foods.
Some eat plants, some eat meat.

Content:
Goat eats grass and leaves.
Cow eats grass and hay.
Fowl eats grain and maize.
Dog eats meat and rice.
Fish eats small worms.
Lion eats meat.

Class activity:
Let's play feeding game.
I will name an animal.
You say what it eats.

Evaluation questions:
What does a goat eat?
Name food for fowl.
What does a dog eat?

Summary:
Different animals eat different foods.

topics.title: Simple cooking
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to wash and peel vegetables.
The pupils should be able to name simple cooking steps.

Introduction:
We eat cooked food every day.
Cooking makes food soft and tasty.

Content:
First wash your hands with soap.
Wash vegetables with clean water.
Peel yams and potatoes.\ Cut vegetables into small pieces.
Put pot on fire.
Add water and salt.
Cook food until soft.

Class activity:
Let's wash and peel potatoes.
Each pupil will wash one potato.
We will peel them together.

Evaluation questions:
What do we do first when cooking?
Name one vegetable we can cook.
Why do we wash our hands?

Summary:
Cooking makes food ready to eat.

topics.title: Food preservation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state why we dry food.
The pupils should be able to list preserved foods.

Introduction:
Some foods can spoil quickly.
We preserve them to last long.

Content:
We dry pepper in the sun.
We dry fish to keep them.
Dried food lasts many weeks.
We store dried food in tins.
Dried pepper makes soup tasty.
Dried fish is used in jollof rice.

Class activity:
Let's see dried pepper and fish.
Touch and smell the preserved food.
Count how many pieces we have.

Evaluation questions:
Why do we dry food?
Name one preserved food.
Where do we store dried food?

Summary:
Drying food helps it last long.

topics.title: Poultry at home
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name poultry animals.
The pupils should be able to state how to care for fowls.

Introduction:
Some people keep fowls at home.
Fowls give us eggs and meat.

Content:
Poultry animals are fowls and chickens.
We keep them in a coop.
Give them water to drink.
Feed them with grain and maize.
Collect eggs every morning.
Clean their home often.

Class activity:
Let's draw a fowl coop.
Each pupil will draw one fowl.
We will label the parts.

Evaluation questions:
What do we give fowls to eat?
Where do fowls sleep?
What do we collect from fowls?

Summary:
We can keep fowls for eggs and meat.

topics.title: Craft with used items
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to make simple toys from used items.
The pupils should be able to state why we reuse items.

Introduction:
We can use old things to make new things.
This helps our environment.

Content:
We can use tins to make cars.
Bottles can become pencil holders.
Cardboard can be made into houses.
We paint and decorate our crafts.
Reusing items reduces waste.
Our crafts can be used for play.

Class activity:
Let's make a car from tin.
Each pupil will bring a clean tin.
We will decorate our cars.

Evaluation questions:
What can we make from bottles?
Name one used item for craft.
Why should we reuse items?

Summary:
We can make nice things from old items.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to answer questions about term work.
The pupils should be able to name things learned this term.

Introduction:
Today we will revise what we learned.
Be ready to answer questions.

Content:
We learned about the market.
We learned about workers and tools.
We learned about planting vegetables.
We learned about animals and their food.
We learned about cooking.
We learned about food preservation.
We learned about keeping fowls.
We learned about craft with used items.

Class activity:
Let's play quiz game.
I will ask questions.
You will raise your hand.

Evaluation questions:
Name one worker you know.
What does a farmer use?
How do we plant seeds?
What food does a goat eat?
Why do we dry food?

Summary:
We learned many useful things this term.
